title: Handoff corridors: mapping engineering, design, legal checkpoints for PRD change approvals
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem: PRD scope changes and last-minute clarifications are creating asynchronous, ad-hoc reviews across eng/design/legal that delay releases and leave acceptance criteria ambiguous. Goal: Define clearly mapped 'handoff corridors'—a small set of deterministic checkpoints and artifacts each discipline must review/approve for PRD changes (minor spec edits, scope reductions, and scope enlargements). This ticket owns the playbook, tooling hooks, and runbook examples to standardize cross-team acceptance for follow-on implementation work.

Scope:
- Create a checklist matrix for three change classes (minor edits, scope trimming, scope expansion) that specifies who must review, required artifacts, expected SLAs, and gating rules.
- Produce two example runbooks (one for a minor UX tweak; one for a model-related scope expansion touching runtime and billing).
- Add a short Confluence template and a PRD change template that auto-populates required artifacts for each corridor.
- Define the notification channels and required metadata in the Linear ticket (labels, reviewer assignments, and evidence links).

Out of scope:
- Building automation integrations (we will document webhook requirements instead); full RBAC enforcement for approvals (handled in a follow-up EpIC).

Success metrics:
- Time-to-approval for PRD changes reduced to <= 3 business days for minor edits, <= 7 days for scope expansion.
- 90% of PRD-change Linear tickets include the required artifact links and at least one cross-team reviewer within 48 hours.
acceptance_criteria: A clear matrix published in Confluence mapping change class -> required reviewers (eng/design/legal) -> artifact checklist
Two example runbooks included in Confluence and linked from the template
Linear PRD-change template created and validated by Design and Legal (UX doc + dataflow diagram + legal checklist)
A brief rollout email + Slack playbook for on-call reviewers and PMs
Stakeholder signoff: Product, Eng Lead, Design Lead, Head of Legal have acknowledged the playbook in a single meeting and provided written thumbs-up in comments
stakeholders: Engineering: Marco Fernández (assignee), Priya Singh (runtime lead)
deliverables: Confluence playbook: 'Handoff corridors for PRD change reviews' (published)
Linear ticket template: PRD-change-template that enforces artifact links
Rollout comms and brief training session recording
